title: Radio frequency readout and control of Ge/SiGe hole spin qubits with a global accumulation gate
authors: Tien-Ho Chang, Chi-Wei Lee, Jian-Chang Zeng, Chia-Hao Wei, Ching-Shiang Wang, Fu-Yuan Gu, Guan-Yu Yang, Ruei-Syuan Chiang, Ho-Chun Wu, Ming-Hao Lee, Ming-Wen Chu, Guang Li Luo, Ta-Chun Cho, Shawn S. H. Hsu, Tzu-Kan Hsiao
abstract: Hole spin qubits in undoped Ge/SiGe quantum well structures have advanced rapidly in performance and scalability. However, stringent multi-layer patterning and overlay requirements of conventional overlapping-gate devices create a bottleneck for academic proof-of-concept experiments involving few-qubit devices. Here we present fabrication and measurements of Ge/SiGe spin qubit devices with a global accumulation gate and single-layer depletion fine gates, which substantially reduce fabrication complexity. With careful design of the gate-2DHG capacitance, we demonstrate RF-based single-shot spin readout and coherent control of two single-spin qubits. We also characterize the spin coherence times and exchange tunability, which are similar to those reported in recent overlapping-gate Ge/SiGe spin qubit devices. By simplifying fabrication without sacrificing performance, our approach offers a more accessible device design for spin-based quantum technology research.
summary: The paper reports on hole spin qubits in Ge/SiGe structures using a novel global accumulation gate design to simplify device fabrication. They successfully demonstrated single-shot readout and coherent microwave control of two qubits while maintaining performance metrics comparable to complex, overlapping-gate devices. This work paves the way for more scalable solid-state quantum computing architectures.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming fabrication bottlenecks associated with conventional overlapping-gate devices when building few-qubit spin quantum processors.
main_result: The authors demonstrated single-shot spin readout and coherent control of two qubits using a simplified global accumulation gate design, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods.
method: They fabricated Ge/SiGe hole spin qubit devices using a novel global-gate structure and employed RF reflectometry for readout and microwave (MW) pulses for coherent manipulation.
model_or_system: The system utilizes hole spin qubits confined in undoped Ge/SiGe quantum well structures. The key innovation is the use of a global accumulation gate combined with single-layer depletion fine gates, significantly simplifying the required lithography compared to traditional overlapping-gate designs.
key_observables: Single-shot spin readout (Pauli Spin Blockade histogram), Rabi oscillation amplitudes/frequencies, and spin coherence times ($T_2^*$).
important_parameters: Global gate capacitance ($\sim 73$ fF); Coherence times ($T_2^*$ up to $\sim 3 \mu	ext{s}$); Exchange tunability (quantified by energy splitting).
main_assumptions: The global-gate design is assumed to maintain the necessary electrical coupling and performance metrics required for high-fidelity quantum operations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, charge stability diagrams from RF readout, histograms showing singlet/triplet populations (SNR=4.6), and spectroscopy plots detailing spin energy levels, Rabi oscillations, and coherence measurements.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the simplified global-gate architecture, then demonstrating single-shot readout via PSB, followed by characterizing coherent control through MW driving, and concluding with measurements of coherence times and exchange coupling tunability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in solid-state quantum computing platforms. The successful integration of advanced qubit control (Rabi oscillations, entanglement tuning) into a simpler fabrication scheme makes the platform more accessible for broader research efforts.
